{{Quote|Palpatine was a pragmatist. As am I.|Roganda Ismaren|<ref name="Age" />}}
'''Roganda Ismaren''' was a [[Human/Legends|Human]] [[Gender/Legends|female]] from [[Alderaan/Legends|Alderaan]], a former [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] [[Jedi Initiate/Legends|Initiate]] who had escaped the [[Great Jedi Purge/Legends|Great Jedi Purge]]. In [[18 BBY/Legends|18 BBY]], she and several other younglings were smuggled to [[Plett's Well]] on the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Belsavis/Legends|Belsavis]], under the guidance of [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]] [[Plett]]. However, their refuge was discovered by [[Galactic Emperor/Legends|Emperor]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]], who sent the [[Dreadnaught/Legends|dreadnaught]] ''[[Eye of Palpatine]]'' to wipe out the Jedi. Although the weapon was disabled, Roganda was captured by [[Inquisitorius/Legends|Imperial Inquisitors]] during the evacuation of Belsavis. Taken to [[Coruscant/Legends|Imperial Center]], Roganda integrated herself into Imperial society, growing into a beautiful woman. Using her good looks and [[Force-sensitive/Legends|Force-sensitivity]], Roganda infiltrated the exclusive [[Imperial Court/Legends|Imperial Court]], eventually becoming one of the Emperor's concubines. During her time as Palpatine's consort, she began an affair with another court member, [[Sarcev Quest]]. When she became pregnant, Roganda submitted herself to the Emperor's mercy, becoming an [[Emperor's Hand/Legends|Emperor's Hand]] and training in the [[Dark side of the Force/Legends|dark side of the Force]]. In [[4 BBY/Legends|4 BBY]], Roganda gave birth to her son, [[Irek Ismaren]], and began to train him as a possible heir to the Emperor. However, upon Palpatine's death in [[4 ABY/Legends|4 ABY]], Roganda did not have the necessary support to make a play for the throne. She retreated back to Belsavis and trained her son for a future attempt to take control of the Empire.

By [[12 ABY/Legends|12 ABY]], Roganda had formulated a [[Ismaren plot|plan]] to reunite the fragments of the Empire. Her son, who had been implanted with a [[subelectronic converter]], used this device to summon the disabled ''Eye of Palpatine'' to Belsavis. With the promise of the warship at her command, she made overtures to various [[Noble/Legends|nobles]] in the [[Senex sector/Legends|Senex]] and [[Juvex sector/Legends|Juvex sectors]] to gain backing for her son as the new Emperor. However, when the ship arrived above Belsavis, Irek found that he could not control it, and the plot fell apart. Roganda and her son made their way back to Coruscant, where she continued Irek's training, recruiting [[Lord/Legends|Lord]] [[Cronal]] to train her son. However, in an argument with his teacher, Irek was stabbed through the head with a [[Lightsaber/Legends|lightsaber]], rendering him brain-dead. Devastated, Roganda refused to accept the loss of her boy, placing him in [[Suspended animation/Legends|suspended animation]] and trying to repair his brain with [[Cybernetics/Legends|cybernetics]]. She also augmented him to become the most powerful [[darksider]] imaginable, installing lightsabers in his wrists, elbows, and knees and using growth hormones to increase his size to three [[Meter/Legends|meters]] in height. In an attempt to bring back Irek's mental faculties, she prepared operational programming and prefabricated memories to install into his destroyed brain. However, before this could be implemented, a [[Groundquake/Legends|groundquake]] awakened Irek from stasis. Driven only by a mindless need to destroy, he used the lightsabers installed into his body to cut his mother to pieces, ending her life.

==Biography==
===Early life===
{{Quote|If I'd followed the strictest traditions of my family I'd have been destroyed, as they and my older brother Lagan were destroyed. As it was, I adapted those traditions.|Roganda Ismaren, to [[Leia Organa Solo/Legends|Leia Organa Solo]]|<ref name="Age" />}}
[[File:Roganda_Ismaren.jpg|thumb|left|200px|Roganda Ismaren during her time as Palpatine's concubine]]
Roganda Ismaren originally hailed from the [[Core Worlds/Legends|Core World]] of [[Alderaan/Legends|Alderaan]].<ref name="EGC" /> Roganda and her brother [[Lagan Ismaren|Lagan]] were the offspring of members of the [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi Order]].<ref name="CotJ" /> Roganda had been trained in the [[Jedi Temple/Legends|Jedi Temple]] until the rise of the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] and the onset of the [[Great Jedi Purge/Legends|Great Jedi Purge]].<ref name="NEGTC" /> To escape the purge, Roganda, her brother, and her parents were taken to the world of [[Belsavis/Legends|Belsavis]] and hidden in [[Plett's Well]], a village founded by the [[Ho'Din/Legends|Ho'Din]] [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]] [[Plett]] as a refuge against the newly founded Empire.<ref name="CotJ" /> While there, Roganda continued her training under Master Plett, developing her Jedi powers.<ref name="DSSB">''[[The Dark Side Sourcebook]]''</ref> As members of the "[[Children of the Jedi]]," Roganda and Lagan hid from Imperial agents<ref name="CotJ" /> until [[18 BBY/Legends|18 BBY]],<ref name="TEC">[[The Essential Chronology (real-world book)|''The Essential Chronology'']]</ref><ref name="DateEye">[[Children of the Jedi (novel)|''Children of the Jedi'']] states that the ''[[Eye of Palpatine]]'' was sent to attack [[Belsavis/Legends|Belsavis]] "thirty years ago." ''[[The Essential Reader's Companion]]'' dates ''Children of the Jedi'' to [[12 ABY/Legends|12 ABY]], giving a date of [[18 BBY/Legends|18 BBY]] for the attack.</ref> when the Jedi refuge was discovered. [[Galactic Emperor/Legends|Galactic Emperor]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]] sent a colossal irregularly shaped [[Dreadnaught/Legends|dreadnaught]], the ''[[Eye of Palpatine]]'', alongside a fighter-wing escort<ref name="CotJ" /> of [[TIE/ln space superiority starfighter/Legends|TIE Fighters]],<ref name="EGtPM">''[[The Essential Guide to Planets and Moons]]''</ref> to Belsavis to wipe out the refugees. Although two Jedi, [[Callista Ming|Callista Masana]] and [[Geith Eris]], disabled the weapon,<ref name="CotJ" /> the TIE fighters [[Attack on Belsavis|attacked]] [[Plett's House]] and the refuge hidden under it, causing minor damage.<ref name="EGtPM" /> With the ''Eye of Palpatine'' out of commission, the Jedi defeated the fighter wing, but since the Empire now knew their location, Plett and the Children of the Jedi were forced to abandon their home.<ref name="CotJ" /> In the chaos of the evacuation from Belsavis, Roganda and Lagan were kidnapped by Imperials, stolen away from their parents. The siblings were presented to the [[Inquisitorius/Legends|Imperial Inquisitor]] [[Ameesa Darys]] who executed Lagan, forcing Roganda to watch. Traumatized by the death of her brother, she resolved to gain enough power that she would never be subjected to the same fate as her sibling.<ref name="TEP" /><ref name="CSWE">{{CSWECite|II|120|Roganda Ismaren}}</ref> Roganda used her fledgling Force powers to escape the Inquisitors and integrate herself into the Empire.<ref name="JvS" />

When Roganda came of age, she developed into a beautiful woman and quickly realized the effect she had on men. While living on the Imperial capital world of [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]], she used seduction and the promise of carnal pleasures to become involved with the elite of Imperial Center. Roganda infiltrated the [[Imperial Court/Legends|Imperial Court]], using her beauty and seeming naivety to play into the court's chauvinistic attitudes. Roganda eventually set her sights on Emperor Palpatine, becoming one of his many concubines and a favored member at court. Due to her [[Force-sensitive/Legends|Force-sensitivity]], she distinguished herself as one of Palpatine's foremost courtesans.<ref name="TEP" /> As a mistress of the Emperor, Roganda was lent to Imperial dignitaries as a temporary gift.<ref name="CotJ" /> During this time, Roganda met [[Sarcev Quest]], a servant of the Emperor and a staple of the court. Handsome and charismatic, Quest became involved with Roganda, and she became pregnant. Knowing that her pregnancy made her a liability due to her role as Palpatine's mistress, she devoted herself to becoming a servant of the Emperor and less disposable to His Imperial Majesty. Her resolve and dedication eventually saw her promoted to one of the [[Emperor's Hand/Legends|Emperor's Hands]], elite [[Dark side of the Force/Legends|dark-side]] users that reported directly to Palpatine. As an Emperor's Hand, Roganda was assigned to seduce Palpatine's enemies and learn their secrets,<ref name="TEP" /> also working as an [[Assassin/Legends|assassin]].<ref name="DSSB" /><ref name="JvS" /> In [[4 BBY/Legends|4 BBY]],<ref name="Irek's Age">[[Children of the Jedi (novel)|''Children of the Jedi'']], Leia states that Irek "had to have been at least four years old" when Leia first encountered Roganda before the Battle of Yavin. This was referenced in "[[The Emperor's Pawns]]," which states that Irek was eight years old at the Battle of Endor in 4 ABY. However, this reference was ignored by later sources, such as ''[[The Essential Guide to Characters]]'' and the ''[[Jedi Academy Training Manual]]'', which sets Irek's age at 14 in ''Children of the Jedi'', which would place his birth in [[2 BBY/Legends|2 BBY]]. This article uses the original 4 BBY date.</ref> she gave birth to her child, [[Irek Ismaren|Irek]], back on Alderaan,<ref name="EGC" /><ref name="JATM">''[[Jedi Academy Training Manual]]''</ref> and began to groom him as Palpatine's heir. She believed that placing her son on the throne would be adequate revenge for the death of her family at the hands of the Empire.<ref name="TEP" />

===End of the Empire===
{{Quote|It's a hotbed of intrigue, dear; just terrible. I'm told they're all at daggers-drawing, my dear. Because of course, whoever can provide him with a child, that child is going to be his heir.|[[Celly Organa/Legends|Celly Organa]], about Palpatine's concubines|<ref name="Age" />}}
Following the birth of her son, rumors abounded that Irek was the Emperor's progeny, and Roganda did not deny them, concealing the identity of his true father to garner further support for her son as a possible heir to the throne.<ref name="TEP" /> While Irek was still a child, Roganda began to train her son in the dark side of the Force, hoping to develop him into a talented Force user.<ref name="CotJ" /> During Irek's training, Roganda came upon the scientific articles "[[The Light Side of the Subelectronic Force]]" and "[[The Universal Energy Field]]" by the Imperial scientist [[Nasdra Magrody]]. In the articles, Magrody speculated about the possibility of implanting a device into a Force-sensitive's brain to allow that person to manipulate technology through the Force. Desiring this power for her son, Roganda kidnapped Magrody.<ref name="Droids">{{Hyperspace|url=hyperspace/member/insideronline/81/indexp7.html|text=Droids, Technology and the Force: A Clash of Phenomena|int=Droids, Technology and the Force: A Clash of Phenomena (article)}}</ref> Shortly after the [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|Battle of Yavin]], when Irek turned five, Magrody implanted his invention, a [[subelectronic converter]], into Irek's brain, allowing the young boy to manipulate technology through the Force.<ref name="CotJ" /> Two years later, at the age of seven, Irek began further training in the dark side of the Force, overseen by Magrody,<ref name="EGC" /> who had a modicum of Force-sensitivity. Magrody also schooled Irek in science, using accelerated learning techniques that he had developed at [[Omwat orbital station]]. Roganda claimed to Magrody that this training was at the Emperor's command, but the Imperial scientist was skeptical that Palpatine knew anything about it.<ref name="CotJ" />

Shortly before the Battle of Yavin,<ref name="BallDate">[[Children of the Jedi (novel)|''Children of the Jedi'']] states Leia Organa was eighteen when she attended the levee, and ''[[The New Essential Chronology]]'' establishes her birth year as [[19 BBY/Legends|19 BBY]]. However, ''[[The Essential Guide to Characters]]'' states that the banquet occurred "two years prior to the Battle of Yavin." The guide also mentions Organa's age of 18, perhaps denoting that this timeline placement was a mistake. Also confusing the issue is that in ''Children of the Jedi'', Leia states that the banquet occurred in the same year that Palpatine dissolved the [[Imperial Senate/Legends|Imperial Senate]], placing it in [[0 BBY/Legends|0 BBY]].</ref> Roganda attended a senatorial banquet on Coruscant,<ref name="Banquet Location">[[Children of the Jedi (novel)|''Children of the Jedi'']] states that the banquet in which Organa first becomes familiar with Roganda took place in the [[Senate Building/Legends|Senate Rotunda]] and was attended by influential members of the Imperial Court, implying that the banquet took place on Imperial Center. However, ''[[The Essential Guide to Characters]]'' places the banquet on Alderaan. This was contradicted when "[[The Princess Leia Diaries]]" depicted the banquet taking place on Coruscant. ''[[The Complete Star Wars Encyclopedia]]'' confirmed that the banquet was on Coruscant.</ref> commemorating [[Princess/Legends|Princess]] [[Leia Organa Solo/Legends|Leia Organa]] as the new [[Senator/Legends|Senator]] from that world.<ref name="CotJ" /> Organa became familiar with Roganda and learned of the rumors about her son from her aunt [[Celly Organa/Legends|Celly]].<ref name="EGC" /> However, Organa was not allowed to speak with Roganda during the banquet, and was kept from doing so by her other aunt, [[Rouge Organa]], who disapproved of the Emperor keeping a harem of concubines.<ref name="CotJ" />

In [[4 ABY/Legends|4 ABY]], Emperor Palpatine was killed in the [[Battle of Endor/Legends|Battle of Endor]].<ref name="RotJ">{{Film|VI}}</ref> This destroyed Roganda's plans for her son to take the throne, as he was only eight years old, and Roganda did not have the support to repel others who were vying for the Imperial throne.<ref name="TEP" /> Roganda also feared that [[Grand Admiral/Legends|Grand Admiral]] [[Mitth'raw'nuruodo/Legends|Thrawn]] had DNA evidence that Irek was not the Emperor's son.<ref name="CotJ" /> When [[Trioculus]] was crowned Emperor<ref name="TEP" /> by the [[Central Committee of Grand Moffs]]<ref name="GoDV">''[[The Glove of Darth Vader]]''</ref> on the claim that he was Palpatine's legitimate son, Roganda knew that she had missed her chance, and she departed Coruscant with her son.<ref name="TEP" /> Roganda later claimed that she sold all of her possessions to escape Coruscant, keeping only a small [[Topaz/Legends|topaz]] ring. She attempted to find refuge on a number of worlds still loyal to the Emperor's memory, but persons there remembered her days as Palpatine's concubine, and she was abused and taken advantage of. Roganda also claimed that her unhappiness during this time caused her to make several bad decisions. By [[5 ABY/Legends|5 ABY]],<ref name="CotJ" /> Roganda had made her way back to [[Belsavis/Legends|Belsavis]] to bide her time until the right opportunity presented itself.<ref name="TEP" />

===On Belsavis===
{{Quote|On other worlds where I thought to take refuge, I've had bad experiences with those who remembered me from the Emperor's Court. And I admit I was&hellip; unhappy enough to do some foolish things in those days.|Roganda Ismaren|<ref name="Age" />}}
[[File:Rogandaismaren.jpg|thumb|right|170px|Roganda during her exile on [[Belsavis/Legends|Belsavis]]]]
In the years since Roganda had resided in Plett's Well, the village had become a hub for [[Smuggler/Legends|smuggling]] activities based on the wealth of supplies left behind in the abandoned settlement under Plett's Well. Now known as "Plawal," the operation was led by the [[town boss]], [[Nubblyk]] the [[Slyte]], who maintained control over the salvage by concealing the tunnels into the underground city. Roganda arranged Nubblyk's disappearance and took possession of his home, a place on [[Painted Door Street]]. To keep the smuggling business of Plett's Well from drawing attention to her location, she orchestrated the disappearance of several smugglers who had worked for Nubblyk, including [[Mubbin]] the [[Whiphid/Legends|Whiphid]] and [[Drub McKumb]], crippling their operation and ensuring that Plett's Well would be left in obscurity and the abandoned settlement left to her devices. Those in the smuggling operation were brainwashed and drugged to use as guards in the tunnels and keep anyone from investigating the abandoned Jedi settlement. Roganda continued to train her son, using Magrody, forcing him to continue Irek's training by imprisoning him on Belsavis and threatening his wife and daughter, [[Elizie Magrody|Elizie]] and [[Shenna Magrody|Shenna]]. Drugged with [[telezan]], Magrody was unable to resist Roganda's orders. By [[8 ABY/Legends|8 ABY]], Irek was well versed in Magrody's lessons, talented enough for an advanced degree in subelectron physics or a position as a droid motivator technician.<ref name="CotJ" />

Around this time, Roganda had recruited around a dozen military types to support her on Belsavis. These soldiers were drawn to her through persuasion and blackmail and worked to protect Roganda's interests. She also rebuilt a semblance of her privileged life that she had enjoyed on Coruscant, obtaining [[vine-coffee]] and expensive perfumes such as [[Lake of Dreams]] and [[Whisper (perfume)|Whisper]]. By the time Irek had turned thirteen, his control over droids and other technology through the subelectronic converter implant was considerable. He was able to alter sensor fields and stayed abreast of all new standard droid models. Roganda brought her son various artifacts of the Jedi from the abandoned settlement, which he mastered. As a mother, Roganda was a strict taskmaster, pushing her son to continually develop his powers.<ref name="CotJ" /> Her efforts formed Irek into a powerful Force user, with abilities that far outstripped her own.<ref name="EGC" /> As a form of rebellion against her demanding nature, Irek would occasionally cause droids in Plett's Well to malfunction and dabbled in substances such as [[yarrock]] that he knew his mother would disapprove of. After Irek had learned all that he could from Magrody, Roganda ended her relationship with the Imperial scientist.<ref name="CotJ" /><ref name="Magrody Death">In [[Children of the Jedi (novel)|''Children of the Jedi'']], Leia states that "Magrody knew far too much to be allowed to live." However, his death is never made explicit in the novel or in his entry in ''The Complete Star Wars Encyclopedia''.</ref>

===Ismaren plot===
{{Quote|I've received reports from operatives in the Senex Sector and the adjoining portions of the Juvex Sector. They say that the heads of six or seven of the old Houses&mdash;the ones who've been lying low, staying out of the border fighting and not committing to the warlords of the Empire&mdash;have all gone 'on vacation'&hellip; without taking their families or their mistresses.''"<br />"''Oh, yeah? Now, that's serious.''"<br />"''This is curious enough, but it coincides almost exactly with the 'vacations' taken by the uncommitted ex-governors of Veron and Mussubir Three, and with representatives of the Seinar Corporation and a high-up member of the Mekuun family. Drost Elegin&mdash;the head of House Elegin&mdash;evidently took his family but left them on Eriadu.|[[Gial Ackbar/Legends|Gial Ackbar]] and [[Han Solo/Legends|Han Solo]] discuss the first evidence of the Ismaren plot|<ref name="Age" />}}
By [[12 ABY/Legends|12 ABY]],<ref name="TERC">''[[The Essential Reader's Companion]]''</ref> Roganda was ready for an attempt at placing her son on the Imperial throne. To do so, she developed a [[Ismaren plot|plot]] involving the aristocratic [[Juvex Lords|lords]] of the [[Senex sector/Legends|Senex]] and [[Juvex sector/Legends|Juvex sectors]]. Using Irek's mastery over machines, she ordered her son to bring the ''Eye of Palpatine'' to Belsavis.<ref name="TEC" /> The Ismarens recruited [[Ohran Keldor]], the original designer of the vessel, into their scheme, so that he could school Irek on the schematics of the ''Eye of Palpatine'', which would allow him to take control of it. From a great distance, Irek was unable to take direct control of the battlemoon, but he activated the signal relay that had been damaged, sending the ''Eye of Palpatine'' back onto its automated mission. The Ismarens hoped that once the device was in range of Belsavis, Irek could take full control over the ship. To keep their plan secret, Roganda arranged the deaths of those who might warn the [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]] about the awakening of the long-dormant [[Superweapon/Legends|superweapon]]. Among those killed was [[Stinna Draesinge Sha]], after Roganda hired the [[Assassin/Legends|assassin]] [[Phlygas Grynne]] to eliminate the scientist and former student of Nasdra Magrody.<ref name="CotJ" />

Using the promise of control over the ''Eye of Palpatine'' as a bargaining chip, Roganda requested financial and military support from [[Senex-Juvex/Legends|Senex-Juvex]] in a campaign to reunite the fractured Empire and place her son as the new Emperor.<ref name="TEC" /> The heads of six or seven [[Noble/Legends|noble]] houses who had tried to stay out of the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]], including [[Lord/Legends|Lord]] [[Garonnin]] and Lord [[Drost Elegin]], answered Roganda's request for a meeting and agreed to come to Belsavis to hear her proposal. Additionally, ex-governors from the worlds of [[Veron Minor|Veron]] and [[Mussubir Three]], and the heads of the [[Mekuun Corporation/Legends|Mekuun]] and [[Seinar Corporation]]s, agreed to meet with Roganda.<ref name="CotJ" />

As Roganda was finalizing negotiations, Leia Organa, now [[Chief of State (New Republic)/Legends|Chief of State]] of the [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]], came to Belsavis with her husband [[Han Solo/Legends|Han Solo]], his copilot [[Chewbacca/Legends|Chewbacca]], and the [[Astromech droid/Legends|astromech droid]] [[R2-D2/Legends|R2-D2]]. Leia and her husband had come to the world to investigate claims from the crazed Drub McKumb, who had escaped his captivity from under Plett's Well and told them of the Children of the Jedi.<ref name="CotJ" /><ref name="TEC" /> Upon their arrival, the group investigated Plett's House, discovering the drugged and brainwashed smugglers protecting the tunnels beneath the house. Worried that Organa and her group would uncover her plot, Roganda had Irek take control of R2-D2 to assassinate the group. However, the plan failed, and Organa recognized Roganda as she spied on them.<ref name="CotJ" /> When Organa confronted the former concubine, Roganda lied to the woman, claiming that she had become a fruit picker, and that her young son had died. Organa was suspicious of Roganda's claims, including her assertion that she had left the Empire behind, but she agreed to conceal Roganda's location on Belsavis, on the belief that she was truly attempting to live in peace.<ref name="EGC" /><ref name="CotJ" />

However, Organa's curiosity eventually uncovered Roganda's plotting, and she pursued the Ismarens and their allies, Drost Elegin, Ohran Keldor, and Garonnin, into the tunnels below Plett's Well. Roganda and her group captured the Chief of State, but her droid, R2-D2, escaped from their grasp when Irek was unable to control the droid due to it being rewired following the first attack. Irek wanted to kill Organa, but Roganda and her allies knew that the Chief of State would serve much better as a hostage, imprisoning her in the tunnels. As more financial backers arrived on Belsavis, Roganda was forced to drug Organa to keep her from interfering. The large contingent of potential supporters included [[Lady/Legends|Lady]] [[Theala Vandron Jr.|Theala Vandron]] of [[Karfeddion/Legends|Karfeddion]], Lord [[Vensell Picutorion]], Lady [[Carbinol]], one of the lords of [[House Sreethyn]], representatives of the [[Mekuun Corporation/Legends|Mekuun Corporation]], and the president of the board of directors of the [[Seinar Corporation]]. Roganda oversaw her son as he charmed their guests and assured them that his control of the ''Eye of Palpatine'' would be the first step to an allied fleet that would put them in a position of power against the New Republic.<ref name="CotJ" />

===The plan falls apart===
{{Quote|I warn you, Madame, the gunnery computer was a semi-independent entity from the central mission control computer&mdash;the Will. If there's been a problem with the Will itself, it may not even let us on board, much less permit us into the central core.''"<br />"''You mean we may not be able to stop the Eye, or control it afterwards?''"<br />"''There is that possibility.''"<br />"''Then wait here. More pragmatism, if there's one thing I learned in getting out of Coruscant ahead of the Rebels, it was: Never be without money.|Ohran Keldor and Roganda Ismaren|<ref name="Age" />}}
[[File:RogandaAndIrek.jpg|thumb|left|200px|Roganda Ismaren and her son during the Ismaren plot]]
As the ''Eye of Palpatine'' became closer to Belsavis, Roganda ordered Irek to overload the central [[Servomotor/Legends|servomotors]] controlling the landing silos to keep anyone from leaving Belsavis so that they could demonstrate the battlemoon's power. However, when the weapon came in range of the planet, Irek found that he could not control it. Unknown to the Ismarens, the [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]] [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]] had damaged the computer core, keeping Irek from tapping into the battlemoon's systems. The Ismarens believed that Irek's inability to control R2-D2 earlier was tied into his struggle to control the ''Eye of Palpatine'', and they summoned Organa to interrogate her. The Alderaanian princess revealed that R2 had been rewired, which caused Keldor and the Ismarens to surmise that the battlemoon had been damaged. As the landing silos had been shut down, the group planned to commandeer Theala Vandron's shuttle to board the ''Eye of Palpatine'' and attempt to repair the weapon.<ref name="CotJ" />

However, Keldor warned Roganda that the central computer onboard, [[The Will]], might not allow them to gain access to the ship. With this information, Roganda took a large case of [[Galactic Credit Standard/Legends|credits]] in the event that their mission failed. As the group readied for their mission, Organa provoked Roganda, causing her to slap the princess, alerting one of the financial backers, Garonnin. Organa called out to the man, claiming that the Ismarens were abandoning Belsavis to the ''Eye of Palpatine''. Irek killed the man with his [[Lightsaber/Legends|lightsaber]], and in the chaos, Organa escaped. Irek and Keldor pursued the princess through the tunnels, but the intervention of Han Solo resulted in Keldor's death. Without Keldor's help, the Ismarens could not fix the ''Eye of Palpatine'', and they were forced to abandon their plans and their potential supporters. Making their way out of the tunnels, Roganda and her son incapacitated the guards watching over Lady Vandron's [[Tikiar (starfighter)/Legends|''Tikiar'']] starship and used it to depart Belsavis. Following their departure, the ''Eye of Palpatine'' arrived above Belsavis, ready to shell the planet to cinders. However, Luke Skywalker and one of his students, [[Cray Mingla]], had activated the self-destruct of the ship, and before it could attack, the battlemoon exploded, to the relief of those still on Belsavis.<ref name="CotJ" />

Roganda made her way to the [[Atravis sector/Legends|Atravis sector]], where heavy concentrations of [[Admiral/Legends|Admiral]] [[Blitzer Harrsk|Harrsk's]] troops had been reported. The New Republic's [[Admiral/Legends|Admiral]] [[Gial Ackbar/Legends|Ackbar]] eventually gathered intelligence on their destination.<ref name="CotJ" /><ref name="TEC" /><ref name="EGC" /> To counteract Irek's abilities with electronics, the Republic planned to alter the schematics of their starfighters and warships to keep them from being sabotaged and to keep Harrsk from using the Ismarens in his attacks against the New Republic.<ref name="CotJ" /> The individuals who had come to Belsavis to listen to Roganda's proposal were not charged for their involvement, due to the fact that they had only listened to Roganda and not acted upon her plans.<ref name="TEC" />

===Lord Nyax===
{{Quote|Very nasty business. It gives even mad science a bad name.|[[Baljos Arnjak]]|<ref name="ELII">''[[The New Jedi Order: Enemy Lines II: Rebel Stand]]''</ref>}}
By [[14 ABY/Legends|14 ABY]],<ref name="CoruscantDate">In ''[[The New Jedi Order: Enemy Lines II: Rebel Stand]]'', the medical droids that operated on Irek Ismaren state that they arrived at the laboratory on Coruscant "thirteen years ago." ''The New Essential Chronology'' dates the events of ''Enemy Lines II'' to 27.5 ABY.</ref> Roganda and Irek Ismaren had settled back on Coruscant<ref name="CSWE" /><ref name="NEC">''[[The New Essential Chronology]]''</ref> and somehow obtained a handful of [[Sith/Legends|Sith]]<nowiki/>scrolls containing information on the ancient art of [[mechu-deru]], of which Irek's brain implant gave him an enhanced mastery.<ref name="TEP" /> These scrolls also contained the secrets of the [[New Sith Wars|Draggulch Period]] [[Dark Lord of the Sith/Legends|Dark Lord]] [[Belia Darzu]].<ref name="ENDSD">''{{Hyperspace|url=hyperspace/member/insideronline/88/indexp2.html|text=''Evil Never Dies: The Sith Dynasties''|int=Evil Never Dies: The Sith Dynasties}}''</ref> In a laboratory inside the [[Bluenek Section]] [[Pasarian Memorial Atmospheric Reclamation Complex Project]]<ref name="ELII" /> on Coruscant, Roganda hired Lord [[Cronal]],<ref name="Droids" /> a former [[Prophets of the Dark Side|Prophet of the Dark Side]],<ref name="JATM" /> and Emperor's Hand<ref name="TEP">{{GamerCite|5|The Emperor's Pawns}}</ref> to continue Irek's training.<ref name="JATM" /> In an effort to make her son more powerful, Roganda had a group of scientists place her son into [[Prison|stasis]]. While in suspended animation, Roganda had the scientists add muscle mass and bone to his frame and also implanted lightsaber blades in his wrists, elbows, and knees.<ref name="NEC" /> Fearing that other Force users might discover them, she arranged to bring [[Ysalamiri/Legends|ysalamiri]] from [[Myrkr/Legends|Myrkr]] to mask their presence.<ref name="ELII" /> However, during one of her son's lessons, Irek lost his temper, initiating a [[Lightsaber duel/Legends|lightsaber duel]] with Cronal.<ref name="JATM" /> Although Irek's skill with a lightsaber was poor,<ref name="EGC" /> records showed that Cronal was killed in the fight,<ref name="ELII" /> but he escaped through the use of [[technobeast]]s<ref name="DoE">{{SW|url=news/the-imperial-warlords-despoilers-of-an-empire-part-3|series=The Imperial Warlords: Despoilers of an Empire|text=Part 3|nolive=1}}</ref> but not before stabbing Irek through the head with his lightsaber.<ref name="JATM" /> Irek was brain-dead, but Roganda and her [[Medical droid/Legends|medical droids]] maintained his autonomic functions and kept his body alive.<ref name="ELII" />
[[File:Lord_Nyax.jpg|thumb|right|Roganda's son, after his transformation into "Lord Nyax"]]
Over the years, Roganda continued to tend to her son, using medical droids to subject Irek to growth hormones and cybernetic stimulation. These efforts increased Irek's size to three meters in height. Armor plates were installed in his head, torso, elbows, and knees, and the missing portions of his brain, mostly those pertaining to human memory, were replaced with [[Cybernetics/Legends|cybernetics]]. Roganda programmed the droids working with her to not record Irek's transformation, keeping her efforts to repair her son hidden. She also arranged to augment his subelectronic converter so that it would stimulate the remaining portions of his brain to make his control over the Force even greater. However, these efforts could not repair Irek, and Roganda became increasingly unstable, desperate to bring her son back. She created operational programming and prefabricated memories in an attempt to fully restore Irek, at least artificially.<ref name="ELII" />

Before the process could be completed, something, most probably a [[Groundquake/Legends|groundquake]], caused ceiling rubble to drop on the the suspended animation chamber, also killing one or more of the ysalamiri. Irek, his brain devoid of anything but his implant, his instincts, some combat programming, and some deep-level motivations like killing Jedi and taking over [[Vergence/Legends|Force nexuses]], awoke and killed his mother, cutting her into approximately eight pieces with his lightsabers. He escaped and eventually adopted the name [[Lord Nyax]], after the [[Corellian/Legends|Corellian]] bogey-man tale.<ref name="ELII" />

===Post-mortem===
In [[27 ABY/Legends|27 ABY]], after Coruscant [[Battle of Coruscant (Yuuzhan Vong War)|fell]] to the [[Yuuzhan Vong]], an infiltration team consisting of Luke Skywalker, [[Mara Jade Skywalker|Mara Jade]], [[Garik Loran]], [[Baljos Arnjak]], [[Bhindi Drayson]], [[Tahiri Veila]], [[Danni Quee]], [[Kell Tainer]], and [[Elassar Targon]], explored the Pasarian Memorial Atmospheric Reclamation Complex Project. They discovered the laboratory and found Roganda Ismaren's dissected remains, confirming her identity after running cell samples against her records in the laboratory files. Her son was eventually hunted down by the group and defeated.<ref name="ELII" />

==Personality and traits==
{{Quote|What is the 'dark side,' Princess? Some of us think that fanatic adherence to every jot and quibble of an antiquated code is, if not dark precisely, at least stupid. And from all I've heard, the 'dark side' seems to be anything that disagrees with the hidebound, divisive, every-tree-and-bush-is-sacred teachings that shackled the Jedi gifts&mdash;and shackled every political body that had anything to do with the Jedi, whether they agreed with them or not&mdash;like an iron chain.|Roganda Ismaren|<ref name="Age" />}}
Roganda was a slender woman with light skin, black hair and black eyes. She was a soft-spoken woman with a high-pitched, lisping speech. As Palpatine's concubine, she was trained to carry herself gracefully, and she retained this attribute years after Palpatine's death. The young woman was seen as a great beauty,<ref name="CotJ" /> which she used to her advantage in the Imperial Court.<ref name="TEP" /> At high-profile events, Roganda wore elaborate outfits adorned with jewels and precious metals. Her long black hair was woven through with silk and lace. However, upon her departure from Coruscant, Roganda lived simply, wearing plain white dresses and keeping her hair free of ornamentation.<ref name="CotJ" />

As a young girl, Roganda witnessed her brother being killed, which badly traumatized her and gave her a strong desire for power that would keep her from her brother's fate.<ref name="TEP" /> After becoming a member of Palpatine's court, Roganda became a skilled manipulator, able to deceive those around her and portray herself in many different guises. Her ability to work behind the scenes allowed her to survive the cutthroat atmosphere of Coruscant. Although Roganda portrayed herself as shy and defenseless, this was an act to keep people underestimating her. Alone and around her son, this personality was replaced with a collected, ambitious attitude. From her time in the Imperial Court, Roganda had been looked down upon for not being of noble birth and a concubine of the Emperor. She remembered these slights many years after departing Coruscant, resenting those who had scorned her. This also added to her desire for power, and the training of her son was an effort to bring them both the power she had always desired.<ref name="CotJ" /> When Irek was killed by Lord Cronal, Roganda could not accept her son's death, keeping him alive and replacing the damaged parts of his brain with computer parts. Over the years, she became increasingly more deranged, unable to cope with the loss of her boy.<ref name="ELII" />

==Powers and abilities==
{{Quote|She doesn't know as much as she thinks she does.|[[Irek Ismaren]]|<ref name="Age" />}}
Roganda was the daughter of members of the Jedi Order and inherited their Force-sensitivity.<ref name="CotJ" /> Although she was trained in the Jedi Temple<ref name="NEGTC" /> and later by Jedi Master Plett,<ref name="DSSB" /> she was still a child when kidnapped by Imperial Inquisitors.<ref name="TEP" /> However, she was strong enough in the Force to escape the Inquisitors who had captured her.<ref name="JvS" /> Her powers allowed her to infiltrate the Imperial Court and become one of Palpatine's favored concubines. Her devotion to her son also led to her becoming one of the Emperor's Hands.<ref name="TEP" /> However, Roganda's son was much more powerful in the Force than she,<ref name="EGC" /> and although she began her son's training,<ref name="CotJ" /> she was forced to pass off further training to other Force users, such as Nasdra Magrody<ref name="EGC" /> and Lord [[Cronal]].<ref name="JATM" />

==Behind the scenes==
{{Quote|She wondered how Roganda had come to the old man in the first place, and whether it was he who had turned her to the dark side, as he had turned Vader and for a time turned Luke, or whether Roganda had sought him out when she saw the fate of Jedi who tried to stay free. Somehow, Leia strongly suspected the latter.|Excerpt from ''Children of the Jedi'' by Barbara Hambly|<ref name="Age" />}}
Roganda Ismaren was created by [[Barbara Hambly]] as the antagonist in the [[1995]] novel [[Children of the Jedi (novel)|''Children of the Jedi'']]. Following the end of the novel, the character and her son escaped and were not seen again in a novel until [[2002]]. ''[[The New Jedi Order: Enemy Lines II: Rebel Stand]]'' by [[Aaron Allston]] detailed Roganda's final fate, killed by her own son. Several reference articles and books expanded Roganda's backstory and detailed her appearances in the novel. One notable reference article, "[[The Emperor's Pawns]]" in [[Star Wars Gamer 5|''Star Wars Gamer'' 5]], gave information on how Roganda had become an Emperor's Hand and a servant of the Emperor. In addition, it also named the true father of Roganda's son, Sarcev Quest, confirming that her son was not Palpatine's . In ''Children of the Jedi'', Leia Organa muses as to how Roganda was turned to the dark side, concluding that she must have gone to the Emperor herself after seeing the fate of other Jedi. "The Emperor's Pawns" confirmed some of this speculation, clarifying that Roganda had gone to the Emperor after becoming pregnant.

Barbara Hambly originally dated ''Children of the Jedi'' to [[15 ABY/Legends|15 ABY]].<ref name="SWG3">[[Star Wars Galaxy Magazine 3|''Star Wars Galaxy Magazine'' 3]]</ref> This date is contradicted in the novel, as Leia Organa claims that she was introduced as a senator 11 years ago. Additionally, several places in the novel claim that Roganda and Irek have been living on Belsavis for 7 years. It also states that Yoda had died "about seven years ago." However, [[The Essential Chronology (real-world book)|''The Essential Chronology'']] and, later, ''[[The Essential Reader's Companion]]'' dated the novel to [[12 ABY/Legends|12 ABY]]. This movement of the timeline allowed the defeat of the ''Eye of Palpatine'', which had occurred "thirty years ago," to happen after the events of [[Star Wars: Episode III Revenge of the Sith|''Star Wars'': Episode III ''Revenge of the Sith'']], which was dated to [[19 BBY/Legends|19 BBY]]. However, this placement affected Roganda's backstory and some of the ages stated in ''Children of the Jedi''. In the novel, Leia states that Irek is "fourteen or fifteen years old," and ''The Essential Guide to Characters'' definitively states that Irek was fourteen at the time of ''Children of the Jedi''. Moving the novel to 12 ABY has invalidated some of these dates.

In ''Children of the Jedi'', the refugee group that are the namesake of the novel are literally "Children of the Jedi," sons and daughters of members of the Jedi Order. Roganda and her brother are stated to be the offspring of Jedi that were escaping the Empire. The novel was written before the release of [[Star Wars: Episode II Attack of the Clones|''Star Wars'': Episode II ''Attack of the Clones'']] and the revelation that the Jedi Order had a taboo on marriage. However, ''[[The New Essential Guide to Characters]]'', published in [[2002]], [[Retroactive continuity|retconned]] the children into [[Youngling/Legends|younglings]] from the [[Jedi Temple/Legends|Jedi Temple]] and stated that Roganda was one of these Jedi children. However, the reference article "The Emperor's Pawns," published in [[2005]], states that Roganda and her brother "were captured, taken from their parents," referencing the backstory from the novel. This article assumes that Roganda and her brother were Jedi Initiates, and the actual children of Jedi.

In the ''[[Jedi Academy Training Manual]]'', the entry on Irek Ismaren states that Roganda and her son escaped into the jungles of Belsavis after the destruction of the ''Eye of Palpatine'' and later booked passage to Coruscant from Belsavis. This directly contradicts ''Children of the Jedi'', which shows the Ismarens commandeering a ship and escaping into the Atravis system.
